name: Bone broth (long-simmered animal-bone stock)
cross_reference: Category 11 (Meat, Poultry, and Eggs) for the animal-bone basis. Placement is PROVISIONAL pending Karen's ratification (candidate alternative: a standalone Category 11 subcategory); recorded as a human-gated outstanding-ledger item.
scope_note: Long-simmered stock made by extracting connective tissue and marrow from animal BONE (beef, chicken, pork). Mechanistically distinct from a vegetable or muscle-meat stock: bone is the body's principal lead reservoir, and lead partitions from bone into the broth during prolonged (often acidulated) simmering, so lead is the priority analyte and a generic stock limit understates the hazard. Certified as its own row, not the generic soups-broths-stocks row. Fish-bone broth (rare) inherits the Category 6 seafood ceilings for arsenic and mercury, which is why marine rows are excluded from this row's safety-net scan by determination rather than by accident. NO GOVERNMENT REGULATES THE EXACT CELL. No credible sovereign sets a contaminant maximum level for bone, bone extract, bone broth, gelatin or collagen: Hong Kong Cap. 132V Note 1 defines its animal commodities as the edible portion after removal of bones (if any) and fat from the meat, so Cap. 132V reaches the flesh and not the bone, and no EU, Codex, FSANZ, US, Canadian or UK instrument reaches bone either. Every numeric cell on this row is therefore a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS from the nearest applicable sovereign animal-tissue value, which is precisely what read-across is for, and the same ruling is applied to every cell of this row rather than cell by cell: the Cap. 132V animal rows anchor total arsenic, total mercury and total chromium, and the FSANZ and EU muscle-meat rows anchor lead and cadmium. A cell is a control here only where no credible regulator sets a value for ANY animal-derived component (nickel, aluminium), or where the pathway is a packaging one confined to a form the instrument does reach (tin).
material: Single-component animal extract. Long-simmered stock made by extracting connective tissue, collagen and marrow from animal BONE (beef, chicken, pork), with adhering meat and fat, water, an acidulant such as vinegar in most formulations, and aromatic vegetables and salt in some. Presented as a refrigerated or frozen liquid, a shelf-stable carton, pouch or can, or a dried powder or concentrate.
components: COMPONENT-LEVEL SAMPLING PLAN. The certified unit is the production lot, and lead is the priority analyte because bone is the animal's principal lead reservoir and the extraction step is the hazard. (1) PRIMARY UNIT: the broth as consumed. A liquid lot is analysed as sold; a dried or concentrated lot is reconstituted to the serving strength printed on the pack and analysed as the prepared broth, with the ratio recorded on the certificate. A composite of not fewer than three retail units per lot, drawn across the run, for all eleven panel cells, with MANDATORY per-lot lead testing rather than skip-lot. (2) SEPARATELY SAMPLED INPUTS, required on any lot whose lead is materially above the line's established baseline and on every new bone supplier before first certification: the incoming bone by species and skeletal site, the adhering meat and fat, the acidulant, the aromatic vegetable fraction where present, and the extraction water. Bone lead varies by animal age and husbandry, so the bone input is the first escalation target and a supplier change is a re-qualification event. (3) EXTRACTION-PARAMETER RECORD, retained with the lot because it drives partition rather than being an analyte: simmer time, temperature and the acidulant concentration and pH. (4) EQUIPMENT AND PACKAGING, the escalation targets for the chromium screen and the nickel, aluminium and tin controls: the stainless-steel kettle, valves and transfer lines with their hot-contact time (the longest of any row in this category), aluminium stockpots and contact surfaces, foil and laminate packaging, and the can where the form is canned. (5) FISH-BONE BROTH, if produced on the line, is out of this row's scope for arsenic and mercury and inherits the Category 6 seafood ceilings; it is sampled separately and never composited with a terrestrial-bone lot.
basis_guard: wet weight|portion ordinarily consumed|product as placed on market|food as listed in Cap 132V|as_sold
basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must be a dietary food maximum level in a comparable as-consumed family (EU wet weight or product as placed on the market, FSANZ portion ordinarily consumed, Cap. 132V food as sold). v1.2 adds the guard this row previously left null. It matters here for the same reason it matters on the soup row: a bone broth is mostly water, so a packaged-drinking-water parametric value would look superficially comparable and is not. The drinking-water and bottled-water rows that sit below several of this row's bindings (lead 5 to 10, cadmium 3 to 7, total arsenic 10, total mercury 1 to 2, total chromium 25 to 100 ug/kg) govern water sold as the sole daily hydration source, and the EU 10/2011 rows below them are specific migration limits into a food simulant. Neither is a food-content ceiling. A cell whose named anchor falls outside the family fails the build instead of publishing a mixed-basis number. SCOPE OF WHAT THIS GUARD ACTUALLY DOES, corrected in v1.2: it refuses the EU 2020/2184, US EPA, US 21 CFR 165.110 and Health Canada drinking-water instruments, the EU 10/2011 specific migration limits, animal-feed maxima, and toy migration limits, because each carries a distinct basis string. It does NOT refuse the Cap. 132V packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water rows, which share the single Cap. 132V basis string with that instrument's food rows and are therefore indistinguishable to a basis regex. Those rows are excluded by the stated ingredient-water determination and are named by id in each affected cell's companion set, not silently dropped.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; COMPOSITE — disclosed read-across from strictest applicable principal-component sovereign ML; never occurrence-derived)

Pb.label: the muscle-meat lead ML binds at 100 ug/kg, and four credible rows converge on that figure (FSANZ meat 100; Cap. 132V meat of cattle, pig, goat and sheep 100; Cap. 132V meat of poultry 100; Cap. 132V edible offal of poultry 100). The lead-accumulating-tissue analog is a LADDER of 100 to 500 across jurisdictions, not the single 500 figure v1.1 disclosed, and its strictest rung equals the adopted binding
Pb.substantiation: Lead is the priority analyte and a NOT-MATERIAL determination is REJECTED on the bone-leaching evidence. Bone is the body's principal lead reservoir (the skeleton holds the large majority of an animal's lifetime lead burden), and published analyses have reported measurably elevated lead in bone broth relative to the water it is made from, consistent with lead partitioning from bone into the broth during prolonged (and frequently vinegar-acidulated) simmering. No credible regulator sets a maximum level for bone broth, bone, gelatin or collagen (the only gelatin and meat-extract MLs on record are non-credible-tier and far looser, 2000 to 7000 ug/kg, so they are not used), so the nearest credible animal-derived anchor is adopted by read-across at 100 ug/kg. v1.2 CORRECTS THE AUDIT-TRAIL ARGUMENT. v1.1 stated the accumulating-tissue analog as a single figure, 'the looser edible-offal ML (500 ug/kg)', and framed the choice as passing over 500 in favour of 100. That overstated the gap by up to fivefold and is not true in every credible jurisdiction. The offal ladder is hk_cap132v_pb_edible-offal-of-poultry_100 at 100, hk_cap132v_pb_edible-offal-of-pig_150 at 150, hk_cap132v_pb_edible-offal-of-cattle_200 at 200 and aunz_sch19_pb_offal_500 at 500, so under Cap. 132V the poultry offal value EQUALS the adopted binding and there is no gap at all for a chicken bone broth. All four rungs are named in the component set so the full ladder is visible in the compiled record, and the binding remains the strictest applicable value, 100 ug/kg. Nothing stricter is applicable: the by-hand scan of every credible live non-infant lead row below 100 ug/kg returns only drinking-water and bottled-water parametric values (5 to 10 ug/kg), the EU 10/2011 plastics specific migration limit (10), and the Cap. 132V Milk and Secondary milk products rows (20 each), none of which is an animal-tissue component of a bone broth. The bone-leaching evidence drives MANDATORY lot-testing surveillance and a ratchet trigger; it does not license a fabricated occurrence value (Method v2.0 forbids occurrence-derivation). If a certified lot's bone-broth lead exceeds this read-across ceiling, that is a surveillance signal, not a basis for loosening the standard toward an offal limit. INGREDIENT-WATER RULING, and a correction to what the basis_guard can actually do. The Cap. 132V packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water rows sit in the SAME basis string as Cap. 132V's food rows ('food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule'), so this row's basis_guard does NOT filter them out even though it does filter the EU 2020/2184, US EPA, US 21 CFR 165.110 and Health Canada water instruments, whose basis strings are distinct. v1.2 corrects the earlier claim that the guard stops packaged-water values generally: the Cap. 132V water rows are excluded by DETERMINATION, not by the guard, and they are now named by id on every cell they could otherwise be read as binding. The determination: packaged drinking water and natural mineral water are a distinct beverage commodity, regulated as the sole daily hydration source and consumed by the litre, and formulation water is an INPUT SPECIFICATION rather than a principal component of the finished product. Certified lines are required to use potable water meeting the applicable national drinking-water standard, verified on the ingredient-water specification, rather than by re-deriving the composite ceiling from a water instrument. Applying a water parametric value as a food-content ceiling would hold a soup or a broth to a limit set for a product with a completely different daily intake, which no sovereign has done. NON-COMPONENT DISPOSITION, run by hand across the whole register rather than through the row's scope regex, because a scope regex can only hide what it does not match. Every credible, live, non-infant, same-basis register row STRICTER than this cell's published value that is not an animal-tissue component is named in this cell's companion set and declined here, by class. (a) BEVERAGE COMMODITIES: the Cap. 132V and EU fruit-, grape- and berry-juice rows (30 to 50 ug/kg lead) and the packaged-water rows, none of which is an ingredient of a bone broth beyond the formulation water dealt with above. (b) PLANT COMMODITIES: the Cap. 132V fruiting-vegetable, preserved-tomato and canned-chestnut rows (50 each), the EU pulse row (cadmium 40) and the Cap. 132V cereal rows. Aromatic vegetables appear in some bone-broth formulations as a flavouring at a few percent and are strained out before packing, so they are a minor formulation ingredient rather than a principal (characterizing or major-mass) component; the product is bone, water and an acidulant, and a broth held to a fruiting-vegetable ceiling would take its limit from a material it does not substantially contain. A bone broth whose formulation is genuinely vegetable-characterized is not this row's product and certifies as a soup or stock under row soups-broths-stocks, where those vegetable values do bind. (c) DAIRY: the Cap. 132V Milk and Secondary milk products rows (lead 20, total mercury 10). Dairy IS admitted as a principal component on the two composite rows of this category, on the mass and characterizing test stated in their scope notes, and it is declined here for the opposite reason under the same test: a bone broth contains no dairy fraction at all. (d) RENDERED FATS: the Cap. 132V edible-fats-and-oils and fat-spread rows (lead 80, total arsenic 100). Adhering and rendered fat is skimmed rather than sold, and edible fats and oils certify under HMTc Category 30 in their own basis. (e) UNDER-36-MONTHS ROWS: the Cap. 132V cereal-based-food and ready-to-eat complementary-food rows (20 each), which route to HMTc Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule and are not applicable anchors for a general-population product.

tAs.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets total arsenic at 500 ug/kg for meat of animal, meat of poultry, edible offal of animal and edible offal of poultry; all four converge on 500, meat of animal is the nearest applicable commodity, and the cell publishes 500 by disclosed read-across. v1.2 replaces a control whose stated reason was false
tAs.substantiation: v1.1 recorded this cell as a bare control on the statement that no credible regulator sets a total-arsenic maximum level for meat, bone or animal-derived stock. THAT STATEMENT IS FALSE and was false at the moment it was published, because Hong Kong had already been admitted to this category's credible-regulator set on 2026-08-17 and Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule item 2 sets total arsenic at 0.5 mg/kg (500 ug/kg) for Meat of animal, Meat of poultry, Edible offal of animal and Edible offal of poultry. The same row already reads across from the same Cap. 132V meat-of-animal family on its total-mercury cell (hk_cap132v_thg_meat-of-animal_50), so a near-neighbour read-across plainly existed and `control` was the wrong tag under Method v2.0, which reserves `control` for a cell where no defensible sovereign numeric maximum AND no supportable near-neighbour read-across exists. The compiler's stricter-unselected safety-net could not catch this because the row's audit_scope had no alternative matching Cap. 132V's commodity phrasing 'Meat of animal'; v1.2 widens the regex. THE NOTE 1 QUESTION, RULED ONCE AND APPLIED TO EVERY CELL. Cap. 132V Note 1 defines the animal commodities as the edible portion after removal of bones (if any) and fat from the meat, so Cap. 132V does not directly regulate a bone-extracted product. That does not make the instrument inapplicable; it makes it a READ-ACROSS rather than a direct ML, which is exactly how this row's live total-mercury cell has always used it and exactly what Method v2.0 prescribes for an unregulated exact cell. The ruling is therefore that Cap. 132V animal rows are the nearest applicable sovereign anchors for a bone-derived stock, adopted by disclosed read-across, and it is applied identically to total arsenic, total mercury and total chromium on this row. The two cells are not resolved in opposite directions off the same instrument family. INSTRUMENTS CHECKED, so the negative half of the claim is auditable: EU 2023/915 and EU 2024/1987 set no total-arsenic ML for meat, poultry, offal, bone or animal-derived stock; Codex CXS 193 sets none; FSANZ Schedule 19 sets total arsenic only for cereal grains, molluscs, crustaceans, fish and seaweed; US FDA, Health Canada and UK dietary instruments set none. iAs.rationale: There is no inorganic-arsenic source in a terrestrial-animal bone broth: no rice, no marine bioaccumulation, and no arsenical-treated plant component. Inorganic arsenic is bounded by the PUBLISHED total-arsenic ceiling of 500 ug/kg on the tAs cell (iAs <= tAs), and reflex speciation is triggered rather than waived. Fish-bone broth (rare) inherits the Category 6 seafood inorganic-arsenic ceiling.
iAs.reference_method: Bounded by the published total-arsenic ceiling of 500 ug/kg (tAs cell, Cap. 132V read-across). REFLEX TRIGGER: inorganic-arsenic speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS on any lot whose total arsenic reaches or approaches the tAs ceiling, on any lot whose total arsenic is materially above the line's established baseline for that formulation, and on any fish-bone broth regardless of total arsenic. v1.2 replaces v1.1's 'no reflex iAs speciation for terrestrial bone broth', which combined with a tAs cell that published no number left the speciation bound circular and numerically vacuous.
iAs.regulatory_basis: No credible regulator sets an inorganic-arsenic content limit for meat, bone or terrestrial animal-derived stock; the credible inorganic-arsenic MLs are scoped to rice and rice products (EU 2023/915), fruit juices and rice-based drinks (EU 2023/915, US FDA apple juice) and seafood (EU 2025/1891). iAs is a species of and bounded by total arsenic (iAs <= tAs), and the total is now a published sovereign read-across of 500 ug/kg rather than an open screen, so the bound is numeric and enforceable.
iAs.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 and EU 2025/1891; Codex CXS 193; US FDA (including the 2023 apple-juice action level of 10 ug/kg, a beverage commodity); FSANZ Schedule 19; Health Canada; UK; HK Cap 132V. None sets an inorganic-arsenic content limit for meat, bone or terrestrial animal-derived stock.

tHg.label: Hong Kong Cap 132V sets total mercury at 50 ug/kg for meat of animal, meat of poultry, edible offal of animal and edible offal of poultry; all four converge on 50 and meat of animal is the nearest applicable commodity, so it binds bone broth's mercury cell by disclosed read-across. Terrestrial animal meat and bone are not a mercury-bioaccumulation matrix, but a sovereign meat ML exists, so the cell is a disclosed read-across rather than a bare screen. A fish-derived bone broth additionally inherits the Category 6 seafood mercury ceiling; the stricter applicable value binds. Value and binding row unchanged from v1.1; v1.2 completes the ladder and states the Note 1 read-across ruling explicitly
tHg.substantiation: HK Cap 132V Part 2 item 12 (Mercury, expressed as total mercury), Meat of animal = 0.05 mg/kg = 50 ug/kg, with Meat of poultry, Edible offal of animal and Edible offal of poultry all at the same figure. Cap. 132V Note 1 defines these commodities as the edible portion after removal of bones (if any) and fat from the meat, so the instrument does not directly regulate a bone-extracted product and this cell is a READ-ACROSS from the nearest applicable sovereign animal-tissue value rather than a direct ML. v1.2 records that ruling in text and applies it identically to the total-arsenic and total-chromium cells of this row, so no two cells resolve in opposite directions off the same Cap. 132V instrument family. Nothing stricter is applicable: the by-hand scan of every credible live non-infant total-mercury row below 50 ug/kg returns drinking-water, bottled-water and natural-mineral-water parametric values (1 to 2), the Cap. 132V Milk and Secondary milk products rows (10 each, not components of a bone broth), and the Cap. 132V vegetable and cereal rows (10 and 20, likewise not components of an animal-bone stock; they bind the two composite rows of this category instead). Methylmercury remains bounded by this total (MeHg <= tHg) and is reflex-speciated on an elevated total-mercury result. INGREDIENT-WATER RULING, and a correction to what the basis_guard can actually do. The Cap. 132V packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water rows sit in the SAME basis string as Cap. 132V's food rows ('food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule'), so this row's basis_guard does NOT filter them out even though it does filter the EU 2020/2184, US EPA, US 21 CFR 165.110 and Health Canada water instruments, whose basis strings are distinct. v1.2 corrects the earlier claim that the guard stops packaged-water values generally: the Cap. 132V water rows are excluded by DETERMINATION, not by the guard, and they are now named by id on every cell they could otherwise be read as binding. The determination: packaged drinking water and natural mineral water are a distinct beverage commodity, regulated as the sole daily hydration source and consumed by the litre, and formulation water is an INPUT SPECIFICATION rather than a principal component of the finished product. Certified lines are required to use potable water meeting the applicable national drinking-water standard, verified on the ingredient-water specification, rather than by re-deriving the composite ceiling from a water instrument. Applying a water parametric value as a food-content ceiling would hold a soup or a broth to a limit set for a product with a completely different daily intake, which no sovereign has done. NON-COMPONENT DISPOSITION, run by hand across the whole register rather than through the row's scope regex, because a scope regex can only hide what it does not match. Every credible, live, non-infant, same-basis register row STRICTER than this cell's published value that is not an animal-tissue component is named in this cell's companion set and declined here, by class. (a) BEVERAGE COMMODITIES: the Cap. 132V and EU fruit-, grape- and berry-juice rows (30 to 50 ug/kg lead) and the packaged-water rows, none of which is an ingredient of a bone broth beyond the formulation water dealt with above. (b) PLANT COMMODITIES: the Cap. 132V fruiting-vegetable, preserved-tomato and canned-chestnut rows (50 each), the EU pulse row (cadmium 40) and the Cap. 132V cereal rows. Aromatic vegetables appear in some bone-broth formulations as a flavouring at a few percent and are strained out before packing, so they are a minor formulation ingredient rather than a principal (characterizing or major-mass) component; the product is bone, water and an acidulant, and a broth held to a fruiting-vegetable ceiling would take its limit from a material it does not substantially contain. A bone broth whose formulation is genuinely vegetable-characterized is not this row's product and certifies as a soup or stock under row soups-broths-stocks, where those vegetable values do bind. (c) DAIRY: the Cap. 132V Milk and Secondary milk products rows (lead 20, total mercury 10). Dairy IS admitted as a principal component on the two composite rows of this category, on the mass and characterizing test stated in their scope notes, and it is declined here for the opposite reason under the same test: a bone broth contains no dairy fraction at all. (d) RENDERED FATS: the Cap. 132V edible-fats-and-oils and fat-spread rows (lead 80, total arsenic 100). Adhering and rendered fat is skimmed rather than sold, and edible fats and oils certify under HMTc Category 30 in their own basis. (e) UNDER-36-MONTHS ROWS: the Cap. 132V cereal-based-food and ready-to-eat complementary-food rows (20 each), which route to HMTc Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule and are not applicable anchors for a general-population product.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation pathway in a terrestrial-animal bone broth and is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg). It is bounded by the total-mercury cell. Only a seafood-derived bone broth carries a methylmercury pathway, and that inherits the Category 6 seafood ceiling.
MeHg.reference_method: Bounded by the published total-mercury ceiling of 50 ug/kg (tHg cell). REFLEX TRIGGER: methylmercury speciation by species-specific isotope dilution GC-ICP-MS on any lot whose total mercury approaches the published total-mercury ceiling, and on any fish-bone broth regardless of total mercury.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible regulator sets a methylmercury content limit for meat, bone or terrestrial animal-derived stock; the credible methylmercury limits are the US FDA CPG 540.600 action level for fish, shellfish, crustaceans and other aquatic animals (1000 ug/kg) and the Cap. 132V fish-species rows (fish, fish balls and fish cakes 500; orange roughy 800; pink cusk-eel 1000; tuna 1200; alfonsino 1500; shark 1600; marlin 1700 ug/kg), every one of which is an aquatic-animal instrument and every one of which is looser than this row's published total-mercury read-across of 50 ug/kg, so none can bind. MeHg is a species of and bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), now a disclosed read-across of 50 ug/kg (HK Cap 132V meat of animal).
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; Codex CXS 193; US FDA CPG 540.600 (methylmercury action level for fish, shellfish, crustaceans and other aquatic animals, 1000 ug/kg); FSANZ Schedule 19; Health Canada; UK; HK Cap 132V fish-species methylmercury rows. None sets a methylmercury limit for a terrestrial-animal bone broth, and every one that exists is scoped to aquatic animals and is looser than the 50 ug/kg total-mercury ceiling published here.

Ni.rationale: No credible regulator sets a nickel maximum level for meat, bone, offal or animal-derived stock. Every nickel row in the register is Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/1987 (regulation_page regulations/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels). The substantive conclusion is unchanged and was independently re-verified: every credible nickel food row is plant-matrix, infant formula, baby food or chocolate, so none reaches an animal-derived stock and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable. Nickel is therefore a mandatory reported cell with no invented ceiling; Tier-2 analyte. INGREDIENT-WATER RULING, and a correction to what the basis_guard can actually do. The Cap. 132V packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water rows sit in the SAME basis string as Cap. 132V's food rows ('food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule'), so this row's basis_guard does NOT filter them out even though it does filter the EU 2020/2184, US EPA, US 21 CFR 165.110 and Health Canada water instruments, whose basis strings are distinct. v1.2 corrects the earlier claim that the guard stops packaged-water values generally: the Cap. 132V water rows are excluded by DETERMINATION, not by the guard, and they are now named by id on every cell they could otherwise be read as binding. The determination: packaged drinking water and natural mineral water are a distinct beverage commodity, regulated as the sole daily hydration source and consumed by the litre, and formulation water is an INPUT SPECIFICATION rather than a principal component of the finished product. Certified lines are required to use potable water meeting the applicable national drinking-water standard, verified on the ingredient-water specification, rather than by re-deriving the composite ceiling from a water instrument. Applying a water parametric value as a food-content ceiling would hold a soup or a broth to a limit set for a product with a completely different daily intake, which no sovereign has done.
Ni.reference_method: Total nickel by closed-vessel microwave acid digestion with ICP-MS on the homogenised as-consumed broth, one determination per production lot, reported on the certificate with no numeric pass/fail. ESCALATION: a result materially above the line's established baseline for that formulation triggers investigation of nickel-bearing stainless-steel kettles, valves and transfer lines (long hot extraction times are the plausible pathway in a simmered stock), of the ingredient water, and of any plant-matrix additions to the formulation, with a confirmatory second lot before release.

Sn.rationale: Inorganic tin is a tinplate migration pathway confined to the canned form; carton (RTD), frozen and refrigerated bone broth have no tin source, so no ceiling is asserted for them. A CANNED bone broth is verified against the canned-foods tin ML, on which three credible regulators converge at 250 mg/kg (250000 ug/kg): Codex CXS 193 (canned foods), FSANZ Schedule 19 (all canned foods) and HK Cap. 132V (canned food other than canned beverages). Instruments checked for a non-canned form: EU 2023/915 (tin appears only as canned-food and canned-beverage MLs), Codex CXS 193, FSANZ Schedule 19, Cap. 132V, US FDA, Health Canada and UK dietary instruments; none sets a tin maximum level for a broth outside a can. The Cap. 132V canned-beverage row (150 mg/kg) is stricter but is not adopted: a ready-to-drink carton broth is not a canned beverage and has no tinplate contact. THE STRICTEST APPLICABLE CANNED-FOOD TIN ML IS THE EU ROW AT 200 mg/kg, NOT THE 250 mg/kg FIGURE v1.1 NAMED. Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 sets tin at 200000 ug/kg (200 mg/kg) for canned foods other than canned beverages, except canned dried and canned powdered products (eu2023_sn_canned_foods_200000, basis product as placed on the market). It is stricter than the three rows v1.1 named as converging at 250 mg/kg (codex_cxs193_sn_canned_250000, aunz_sch19_sn_canned_250000, hk_cap132v_sn_canned-food-other-than-canned-beverages_250000), it is a credible-regulator maximum level in a basis this row accepts, and it was neither named nor dispositioned. This defect was found by hand during the v1.2 remediation and NOT by the compiler safety-net, because the soups row's audit_exclude_scope contained the term `beverage`, which matched the phrase 'canned beverages' inside the EU row's own scope string and suppressed it from every scan; the same class of regex self-defeat the v1.2 audit identified elsewhere. The term is removed. The canned form is verified against the EU value, and the EU instrument's own carve-out for canned dried and canned powdered products is independent confirmation that a tin maximum level does not reach a dry soup mix or a bouillon powder. Stricter still, and disclosed rather than adopted because they reach a different form: canned beverages at 100 mg/kg (eu2023_sn_canned_beverages_100000) and at 150 mg/kg (hk_cap132v_sn_canned-beverages_150000). Where a certified product is a canned drinkable broth presented as a beverage rather than a canned food, the canned-beverage value is the applicable one and the stricter of the two applicable rows governs; no single number is asserted across forms.
Sn.reference_method: Total tin by closed-vessel microwave acid digestion with ICP-MS on the homogenised as-consumed broth, one determination per production lot. A canned lot is verified against the canned-foods tin ML named in companion_ml. ESCALATION: any measurable tin on a non-canned form triggers packaging-source investigation (can or lid substitution on a shared line, tinned-solder contact, or a tin-bearing additive), with a confirmatory second lot before release.

Al.rationale: No credible regulator sets an aluminium maximum level for bone broth, for any animal-derived stock, or for any animal-tissue component of one. Instruments checked: EU 2023/915 and EU 2024/1987 (no aluminium entry), Codex CXS 193 (no aluminium entry), FSANZ Schedule 19 (aluminium appears only as infant-formula MLs of 500 and 1000 ug/kg, which are Category 1 scope), Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule (no aluminium entry), and US FDA, Health Canada and UK dietary instruments (no aluminium ML). Aluminium reaches the credible register only in basis families that cannot anchor a food-content cell: drinking-water parametric values (EU 2020/2184 and US 21 CFR 165.110 at 200 ug/L, Health Canada at 2900 ug/L), food-contact-material specific migration limits (EU 10/2011, a migration figure into a simulant), and toy migration limits. Permitted-additive maxima for aluminium-containing additives exist only in non-credible-tier instruments and are additive-use levels rather than contaminant ceilings. Aluminium is therefore a mandatory reported cell with no invented ceiling; Tier-2 analyte.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by closed-vessel microwave acid digestion with ICP-MS on the homogenised as-consumed broth, one determination per production lot, reported on the certificate with no numeric pass/fail. ESCALATION: a result materially above the line's established baseline for that formulation triggers investigation of aluminium stockpots, kettles and contact surfaces, of foil and laminate packaging including pouch and carton liners, and of any aluminium-containing additive, with a confirmatory second lot before release.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium is a screen, not a protective ceiling: the value records the sovereign total-chromium ML (Cap. 132V meat of animal, 1000 ug/kg) while the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), which is not stable in this matrix. The cert standards renderer is the consumer that excludes a screen cell from the firm-limit count it displays; the deterministic publication gate in this repo (tools/standards/audit-compiled-standards.mjs) counts screen cells toward its own firm total, so the two counts differ by design and neither is wrong. The escalation rule is equipment-leaching investigation, not a toxicological exceedance.
Cr.basis: read-across from the sovereign total-chromium animal-meat ML (Cap. 132V, food as sold, applied at face value to the as-consumed broth)
Cr.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets total chromium at 1000 ug/kg for meat of animal and for meat of poultry, the nearest applicable sovereign animal-tissue value for a bone-derived stock; the cell publishes it as a SCREEN. v1.2 replaces a control whose stated reason was false
Cr.substantiation: v1.1 recorded this cell as a bare control on the statement that no credible regulator sets a total-chromium maximum level for bone broth. THAT STATEMENT IS FALSE, and it is the same statement that v1.1 itself identified as false and corrected on the other two rows of this category: both composite rows carry the sentence 'v1.0 recorded this cell as a bare control on the statement that no credible regulator sets a total-chromium maximum level ... That statement is false following Hong Kong's admission to the credible-regulator set on 2026-08-17.' Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule item 7 sets total chromium at 1.0 mg/kg (1000 ug/kg) for Meat of animal and for Meat of poultry. A published standard that retains, on a live row, a factual claim it documents as false elsewhere in the same compiled directory is the single easiest thing for opposing counsel to put in front of a jury, so the falsehood is corrected rather than preserved and the v1.1 note that overclaimed the correction is itself corrected (see _doc_v1_1 and _doc_v1_2). Cap. 132V Note 1 excludes bone from these commodities, so this is a disclosed READ-ACROSS from the nearest applicable sovereign animal-tissue value, ruled once for this row and applied identically to total arsenic and total mercury. The looser and stricter Cap. 132V total-chromium rows are disclosed and not adopted for opposite reasons: meat of poultry at 1000 is equal, and vegetables other than pulses at 500 and pulses, cereals and fish at 1000 are not components of an animal-bone stock (they bind the two composite rows instead). Nothing stricter is applicable: the by-hand scan of every credible live non-infant total-chromium row below 1000 ug/kg returns the EU 10/2011 plastics specific migration limit (10), drinking-water, bottled-water and natural-mineral-water parametric values (25 to 100), and the Cap. 132V vegetable row (500), none of which is an animal-tissue component and all of which the basis_guard would refuse. IT PUBLISHES AS A SCREEN: dietary chromium is overwhelmingly trivalent (an essential nutrient) and the health-relevant hexavalent species is separately determined not material in a cooked, wet, protein-rich broth (Cr-VI cell, speciation-bounded), so the value is not protective as a standalone total-element ceiling. Total chromium remains mandatory on every lot. ESCALATION: a result approaching the screen value is treated as a stainless-steel equipment-leaching signal, investigated against kettle and transfer-line contact time and temperature (a bone broth simmers for many hours, which is the longest hot-metal contact of any row in this category), with a confirmatory second lot before release, and not as a toxicological finding. The Cap. 132V packaged-drinking-water and natural-mineral-water rows sit in the SAME basis string as Cap. 132V's food rows ('food as listed in Cap 132V Part 2 Schedule'), so this row's basis_guard does NOT filter them out even though it does filter the EU 2020/2184, US EPA, US 21 CFR 165.110 and Health Canada water instruments, whose basis strings are distinct. v1.2 corrects the earlier claim that the guard stops packaged-water values generally: the Cap. 132V water rows are excluded by DETERMINATION, not by the guard, and they are now named by id on every cell they could otherwise be read as binding. The determination: packaged drinking water and natural mineral water are a distinct beverage commodity, regulated as the sole daily hydration source and consumed by the litre, and formulation water is an INPUT SPECIFICATION rather than a principal component of the finished product. Certified lines are required to use potable water meeting the applicable national drinking-water standard, verified on the ingredient-water specification, rather than by re-deriving the composite ceiling from a water instrument. Applying a water parametric value as a food-content ceiling would hold a soup or a broth to a limit set for a product with a completely different daily intake, which no sovereign has done.

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is reduced to Cr-III in a cooked, wet, protein-rich broth; a Cr-VI result is an artifact of the total-chromium screen. No credible regulator sets a Cr-VI food ML.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Cr-VI is not measured routinely; total chromium (Cr cell) is the reported screen at 1000 ug/kg and bounds any hexavalent fraction. REFLEX TRIGGER: Cr-VI speciation by ion-chromatography ICP-MS only where a total-chromium result approaches the screen value AND the equipment-leaching investigation does not account for it.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No credible regulator sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any food; Cr(VI) reduces to Cr(III) in a cooked, wet, protein-rich broth and any Cr(VI) signal is an artifact of the total-chromium screen. Cr(VI) is a species of and bounded by total chromium (Cr-VI <= total Cr), now a published screen read-across of 1000 ug/kg (HK Cap 132V meat of animal), so the bound is numeric rather than open.
Cr-VI.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; Codex CXS 193; US FDA; FSANZ; Health Canada; UK; HK Cap 132V — none set a hexavalent-chromium content limit for food.
